meaning: Planning associations only. These entries do not change current workshop coverage or claim that a lab has been built.

modules.title: Build and publish the repair API
modules.result: The same versioned image can run locally and be pulled from a private registry.
modules.activity: Start with a tiny Python API and one worker from the same repository. Build an image locally or with an ACR quick task, inspect its tag and digest, then push/pull it. Add one source-triggered build after the manual path works. Use one simple build path first; multi-step tasks, timers, signatures, ABAC and private networking are short extensions or design checks.

modules.title: Release the API without breaking the report form
modules.result: A user submits a repair report through a working HTTPS endpoint; a bad release can be rolled back.
modules.activity: Use Container Apps as the main host. Compare single and multiple revision behavior, route a small traffic share to a test revision and move a stable label URL. Set the listening port and environment values explicitly. An App Service slot deployment is an alternative-host exercise using the same image, not another required production component. Deployment-labels mode is a preview reference or optional demo.

modules.title: Save a report and show its current status
modules.result: The form returns a report ID and the status page reads the right repair record.
modules.activity: Store repair jobs in Cosmos DB. Use Python SDK clients, a deliberate partition key and point reads. Compare one partition-targeted query with a cross-partition query, inspect RU charges and change an unnecessary index. A short consistency exercise explains what a user may read after an update. Discuss multi-region guarantees from a supplied scenario rather than deploying several regions solely for the exercise.

modules.title: Process repair work reliably in the background
modules.result: The API acknowledges quickly; workers complete jobs without applying the same repair twice.
modules.activity: Send work to Service Bus and return HTTP 202 plus a status location. Let worker replicas compete on one queue. Crash a worker before completion, observe redelivery and make the operation idempotent. Add a dead-letter recovery path, one topic with independent subscribers and one property filter. Scale the worker from the queue backlog with KEDA. Sessions, scheduled work, deferral, broker transactions, request/reply and an outbox are focused variants of this flow, not all mandatory features of the repair app.

modules.title: React when a resident uploads a photo
modules.result: A photo upload is associated with its report and produces a visible processing status.
modules.activity: A BlobCreated event reaches a Python Function through Event Grid. The handler accepts the event quickly and hands slow work to the existing worker. Add event-type/subject filtering, retry-safe processing and dead-letter storage. Inspect a failed delivery. Use a small Timer or Storage Queue function as a binding comparison only; do not introduce extra queues into the main flow just to demonstrate every trigger.

modules.title: Give each component only the settings and access it needs
modules.result: The API and worker read configuration securely; a deliberate permission error is diagnosable.
modules.activity: Use managed identities, narrow data-plane roles, Key Vault for a real demonstration credential and App Configuration for ordinary settings. Compare a fresh SDK read with a cached or version-pinned value. Rotate the demonstration credential in both the target and vault, then refresh its consumers. Load a key/label pair and refresh a watched setting. Use a feature flag to expose the new search page. Private endpoints and federation are optional infrastructure extensions, not prerequisites for the first successful request.

modules.title: Follow a slow or failed report through the system
modules.result: A learner can explain where a request failed using traces and a small set of log queries.
modules.activity: Instrument API and worker with OpenTelemetry, give them distinct service names and propagate trace context. Observe request and dependency spans, a log and a metric. Write KQL that filters failures, groups requests, calculates durations, joins related telemetry and plots time buckets. Break one permission or dependency and find it again. Sampling and ingestion-cap exercises use controlled test traffic and configuration comparisons rather than silently dropping evidence during the main debugging exercise.

modules.title: Optional hosting branch: run the same API and worker on AKS
modules.result: The existing images run behind Kubernetes Services and can be investigated with kubectl.
modules.activity: Reuse the API/worker; write Deployment and Service manifests, probes and requests/limits. Roll out and undo an image change, test a selector or target-port error, inspect previous logs and compare pod scaling with node capacity. Add workload identity and a mounted secret in a later step. Namespace permissions, quota/LimitRange, NetworkPolicy and shared volumes are optional variants. DaemonSets, GPU placement, CNI choices and every Service type are discussion or isolated examples unless a real requirement emerges. This branch is needed for practical AKS coverage; it is not needed to finish the main repair app.

modules.title: Create a searchable library of previous fixes
modules.result: Staff can retrieve a known repair article, filtered by a useful category such as electrical or plumbing.
modules.activity: Reuse the running API and authentication from workshop 1. Store curated knowledge articles and supplied embeddings in PostgreSQL. Load rows in bulk, parameterize reads and use an ordinary index for metadata. Use a bounded Python connection pool and secure database access. The source of truth is the article library; Cosmos DB remains the source of truth for live repair jobs.

modules.title: Find similar problems and compare search quality
modules.result: “The street lamp is dark” can find an article titled “Outdoor light does not turn on.”
modules.activity: Use supplied embeddings so no model API is needed. Establish exact nearest-neighbor results, then compare HNSW and IVFFlat on the same question set. Explain cosine, L2 and dot product with tiny numeric examples. Apply metadata filters and compare recall/latency. An optional Cosmos vector branch searches solved repair records or the same copied test fixture to compare indexing policies; it is an alternative retrieval experiment, not a second compulsory copy of the article database.

modules.title: Serve repeated searches quickly without showing stale answers
modules.result: A repeated search becomes a cache hit, and an edited article does not remain wrong indefinitely.
modules.activity: Add Redis cache-aside for article/search results, explicit TTLs and invalidation after updates. Measure hit rate, misses and evictions; simulate a popular key expiring. Start with ordinary caching. An optional semantic-cache branch uses compatible Redis vector search and a clear similarity threshold to reuse stored suggestions for paraphrases. FLAT/HNSW and hash encodings belong to that branch; they are not required merely to cache an article by ID.

modules.title: Keep suggestions synchronized when repair records change
modules.result: A solved repair becomes searchable and its cached status is invalidated without the API publishing a second event for every write.
modules.activity: Consume Cosmos change feed with a Python Function or Python pull client. Maintain progress, tolerate repeated batches and update a derived search entry or invalidate a cached repair status. Run independent consumers for indexing and cache invalidation; use a separate named consumer/checkpoint group for each job. Do not model these as one shared worker group if each needs every change. Explain latest-version omissions and explicit deletion/tombstone handling. Native Change Feed Processor names/APIs are conceptual comparisons because the native processor libraries in the linked material are .NET/Java, not a Python client to implement in this lab.

modules.title: Measure and fix a slow search under realistic concurrency
modules.result: A learner can separate slow connection setup from slow SQL and demonstrate whether a chosen change helped.
modules.activity: Run repeatable searches with fixed data and concurrency. Record P95 latency, recall, pool waits, memory pressure and disk reads. Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE, tune one index search parameter and compare before/after. Test client pooling against repeated new connections; optionally compare built-in PgBouncer. Resource-tier changes are estimates or a controlled extension after finding a bottleneck. Exact SKU ratios, ports, dimension ceilings and defaults remain short reference checks rather than separate app features. Reuse workshop 1 tracing/KQL to explain the measurements.
